name: autotrace
why: Turns bitmaps into vector outlines, a transform from pixels to geometry that is neat but a long-standing, fairly ordinary tool.

brief.what_it_is: AutoTrace is a command-line program that converts bitmap images into vector graphics. It reads raster formats such as BMP, TGA, PNM/PPM/PGM/PBM, and anything ImageMagick can read, then writes vector output in formats including PostScript, SVG, xfig, SWF, EMF, DXF, CGM, MIF, and sk, plus output through pstoedit. The homepage describes it as a free alternative to commercial tools like CorelTrace or Adobe Streamline.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says the aim is 'the development of a freely available application with a functionality similar to CorelTrace or Adobe Streamline', and hopes it will become 'better than all commercially available programs'.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the tracing mechanism in detail. It mentions median-cut colour quantization, despeckle filtering, and centerline tracing, and says outlines are fitted with curves. The contributions list says the core fits outlines and that the current code traces each outline twice.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says AutoTrace ships as source code and some binaries, and that other platforms must compile it themselves. The steps are to download the archive from the SourceForge files page, unpack it, and run make. No runtime, account, or configuration is described. The page does not list the make command as a verbatim command line.
brief.standout: It is an early, open-source take on the pixel-to-geometry problem, and its homepage carries a long, candid list of similar projects and research references (Schneider's Phoenix curve fitting, SUSAN denoising, color quantization papers). It also served as the backend for mftrace and TeXtrace, which convert bitmap fonts to outlines.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest release on the homepage is version 0.31.1, dated 11/09/02. The homepage's 'Last modified' line is 12/12/16. The Download section says 'AutoTrace 0.31.1 (no support by me)', and the Bugs section is a bare '?!'. The homepage is an old SourceForge-era site, and the news items stop in 2004. The scout note calls it a long-standing, fairly ordinary tool.
brief.caveats: The homepage has no documentation beyond online help. Building it from source is the only route on most platforms. The contributions list says whole pictures must fit in memory, and the page calls ImageMagick input 'very slow for loading big images'. The author says he does not support the 0.31.1 release. The page includes a 2002 note about an earlier rival (ScanFont). Licence: GNU GPL, per the homepage.
quotes: The aim of the AutoTrace project is the development of a freely available application with a functionality similar to CorelTrace or Adobe Streamline.
AutoTrace is free software. AutoTrace is distributed under the term of GNU GPL.
Currently there is no documentation other than the online help.
